about: Claims map (docs/CLAIMS.json). Each entry binds a claim made in the documents to the test that exercises it on the production code path, or says that none does. Validated by CHATMCP-HUB/tests/verify-claims-map.mjs; see docs/CLAIMS.md.

claims.claim: An installed and enabled skill reaches the model.

source.quote: install reviewed skills

claims.seamNote: Real AgentRunner, real PluginManager and real GitHub registry install path; only the model (a capturing provider) and the GitHub HTTP transport are scripted. A small skill reaches the model whole in the index of the conversation; a bigger one is a line in the index and its text arrives once after the model calls skill_load. Run again against a copy of lib/ with the v3.9.0 defect put back, which must fail.

claims.claim: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md of the workspace are loaded into the agent's instructions with a hard cap of 8,192 bytes, read only inside the workspace, and cannot change what the permission gate decides.

source.quote: giới hạn cứng **tối đa 8.192 byte**

claims.seamNote: The loader runs on real files in temporary workspaces (links, junctions, a 2 GiB file, binary files). The block is delivered through the real AgentRunner (only the model and a minimal tool session are scripted) with a mutation check, and a hostile AGENTS.md is run through the real HubManager, PermissionGate and LocalTools in Review, Read Only and Autonomous; verify-e2e-prompt-budgets does it again through a real Hub process.

claims.claim: The project instructions and the skill index (with the definition of skill_load) take at most 10% and 5% of the history budget the model's window leaves, and together at most half of what is left above the 1,000-token floor, whatever the window (an unknown one included), so they do not take the history of a run under the floor on which a known window is refused.

source.quote: tối đa **10% lịch sử dự toán**

claims.seamNote: The allowance is checked by hand and over every history from 0 to 60,000 tokens; then the real AgentRunner runs a busy project (spawn tools, check suggestions, a plan) on windows of 11,000 to 200,000 tokens and an unknown one, only the model and a minimal tool session scripted: the cap of every window is the allowance of the policy the SAME run has with the guidance switched off, the history budget never goes under the floor, and the text of the run with the guidance is the text without it plus the block and one sentence of the rules. verify-skill-on-demand does it again with 130 KB of project files, four skills and the real PluginManager, recomputing the budget from what the provider received, and verify-e2e-prompt-budgets through a real Hub process at 16,384 tokens.

claims.claim: The owner can switch the loading of AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md off in Settings: the choice is saved, applies from the next run of every runner, and the environment variable CHATMCP_PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS decides over it.

source.quote: lưu cùng dữ liệu Hub, áp dụng từ lượt chạy kế tiếp

claims.seamNote: A real Hub process (real routes with the bearer, CSRF and Origin layers, the saved store, the real runner and permission gate) and a scripted model server: what the model server is sent after the choice changes, a change while an approval is pending, a restart, the environment variable on and off, a damaged file. verify-project-instructions-setting runs the real AgentRunner, a pooled chat in its own worktree and a coding worker whose runners exist before the choice changes, and ui/e2e/project-instructions.spec.mjs flips it from the real page.

claims.claim: A skill too big for the index is read through skill_load: bounded, once per load, with the Hub's redaction, and without any effect on permissions.

source.quote: mỗi lần nạp tối đa 16 KiB, một lần cho mỗi lần gọi

claims.seamNote: The index and the loader on their own, then the real AgentRunner and the real PluginManager (only the model is scripted): the text arrives once per load, a pooled worker is offered the tool, and a hostile skill is run through the real HubManager, PermissionGate and LocalTools in three modes.

claims.claim: Code intelligence answers from the language server tier through the production chain.

source.quote: supported language servers

claims.seamNote: Real StudioWorkspace -> LocalTools -> CodeIntelligenceEngine -> CodeIntelligence -> LspProcess; only the language-server child process differs (a protocol-faithful stub always, the real servers when installed).

claims.claim: A Tree-sitter adapter handed to LocalTools reaches the code-intelligence engine.

source.quote: Tree-sitter WASM grammars

claims.seamNote: Real StudioWorkspace and real LocalTools driven through the registered tools; the parser is a recording stand-in, and the recording is what proves the injected adapter was reached.

claims.claim: In Read Only a shell command runs only when the classifier recognises it as read-only.

source.quote: Shell commands run in this mode only when the command classifier (`lib/command-analysis.mjs`, `lib/read-programs.mjs`) positively recognises them as read-only

claims.seamNote: Bypass corpus through the real classifier, real LocalTools and real PermissionGate on real files; a positive control shows the same commands DO write when approved in Review.

claims.claim: After the Hub is killed during a command, the command is not run again by the Hub.

source.quote: the Hub must not automatically replay ambiguous mutations

claims.seamNote: A real Hub process killed with SIGKILL / TerminateProcess, restarted on the same state folder; the number of lines a script appended to a file says how many times it ran.

claims.claim: The Hub takes a checkpoint before an agent edit and restores it only if the file is still as reviewed.

source.quote: Hub tự lưu một checkpoint của các file sắp đổi

claims.seamNote: A real Hub process over HTTP: edit approved in Review, checkpoint listed, diff reviewed, a stale restore refused with 409, the restore applied when the file is as reviewed.

claims.claim: Every Hub API route needs the per-launch bearer except the named exceptions.

source.quote: every API request (reads and the live event streams included) must carry a per-launch secret as `Authorization: Bearer`

claims.seamNote: A real Hub process: every route found in hub.mjs is requested without the secret; tested routes must equal declared routes. The exceptions are pinned (see docs/THREAT-MODEL.md, RR-2 and RR-3).

claims.claim: The bearer protects against other accounts, restricted processes and web pages (not against same-user programs).

source.quote: This boundary protects against other Windows accounts, sandboxed processes that cannot read your files, and web pages in your browser.

claims.seamNote: Real Hub: session file ACL (SDDL has only the owner), Host/Origin/CSRF layers refuse web pages, the secret is not inherited by child processes. Not tested: a second Windows account, a restricted-token process. The two forged-Origin read routes are an open exception (docs/THREAT-MODEL.md RR-2; verify-threat-model.mjs observes it).

claims.claim: Secret-shaped text in a tool result never reaches the text the Companion types into chatgpt.com.

source.quote: masks text that is shaped like a secret before it is sent

claims.seamNote: The real BrowserRunner runs start -> poll -> claim -> sent -> reply as the extension drives it; the assertions read the text poll() and claim() return. Only the tool server is a stand-in. Pattern-based: secrets without a recognisable shape are not caught.

claims.claim: A tool result that names .env*, *.pem, *.key, id_rsa* or another protected file is withheld whole.

source.quote: withholds what a tool read from

claims.seamNote: Same real BrowserRunner flow, including a protected file read through a non-local tool.

claims.claim: With Review before send on, a tool result is held until the owner decides and is never offered to the Companion before Approve.

source.quote: offers an optional **Review before send**

claims.seamNote: A real Hub process over HTTP with the Companion played through its own routes and the person through the dashboard routes (with the Hub secret); the tool that runs is the real local.read_file.

claims.claim: ChatMCP's own code is licensed under Apache-2.0 (LICENSE, NOTICE, README, installer payload).

source.quote: ChatMCP's own source code is licensed under the **Apache License, Version 2.0**

claims.seamNote: Reads the real README, LICENSE and NOTICE; the installer payload requirement is checked in the script and in scripts/tests/Test-InstallerPayload.ps1 (a CI step). 15 seeded defects are each reported.

claims.claim: A pull request commit without a Signed-off-by trailer fails the DCO check.

source.quote: every commit of a pull request needs a Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off

claims.seamNote: The real scripts/check-dco.mjs against real temporary Git repositories, plus the properties of .github/workflows/dco.yml. Not run: the workflow on GitHub.

claims.claim: The OpenAI Responses adapter validates messages, binds tool results to calls and requires a terminal SSE event.

source.quote: supports validated text/function call messages, tool result correlation, bounded SSE with terminal completion

claims.seamNote: The real adapter module and the real GatewayProvider; only fetch is scripted. The separate function-probe path of the same sentence is not exercised here.

claims.claim: Cost totals are shown only from known usage and owner-supplied rates.

source.quote: No guessed total is shown when usage, pricing or failed-attempt billing is unknown.

claims.seamNote: Pure functions of lib/model-cost.mjs with no collaborators; the UI that shows the total is not exercised by this test.

claims.claim: Project check discovery lists checks without running them.

source.quote: Read-only project check discovery can list Node, TypeScript, Python, Rust, Go and Playwright checks.

claims.seamNote: The real discoverProjectChecks on real temporary projects. Covers Node, TypeScript, Python, Rust and browser checks and that nothing runs; there is no Go case.

claims.claim: The evaluation CLI runs fixtures, saves a revision-bound report and reports no live-model result.

source.quote: A deterministic evaluation CLI runs existing real-process regression fixtures and saves revision-bound reports; it does not fabricate live-model results.

claims.seamNote: Spawns the real tests/evaluate.mjs process and reads the report it wrote.

claims.claim: Passing test receipts and file hashes are invalidated after a potentially mutating edit.

source.quote: Previously passing tests and file hashes are invalidated after potentially mutating edits.

claims.reason: No test drives the real agent loop through an edit and then looks at the receipts: tests build the receipt objects by hand.

claims.claim: The owner accepts each objective criterion against fresh first-party receipts.

source.quote: an owner accepting each objective criterion

claims.reason: verify-objective-acceptance.mjs calls the real acceptObjectiveCriterion with hand-written receipts (progress objects), not receipts produced by the agent.

claims.claim: Encrypted provider profiles, defaults, role overrides and revision checks.

source.quote: AI Settings can manage multiple encrypted local provider profiles

claims.reason: Not audited for the production seam: verify-profile-routing.mjs uses a fake primary runner; encryption at rest and the revision check on resume are not shown on a production path.

claims.claim: Context budgets include instructions, tool schemas and reserved response space.

source.quote: Model-specific context budgets estimate instructions, tool schemas and reserved response space

claims.reason: Not audited: the candidate suite has not been checked for doubles.

claims.claim: Publishing needs a green run on the exact release commit.

source.quote: Publication requires success on the **exact release commit**

claims.reason: Enforced by .github/workflows/publish-v3.9.0.yml; no suite reads or runs it.

claims.claim: The Companion ZIP is verified against the installer payload in the release workflow.

source.quote: is packaged from the matching source/payload and verified in the release workflow

claims.reason: Done by scripts/Build-BrowserCompanion.ps1 -VerifyInstallerPayload in the CI and release workflows; no Node suite exercises it.

claims.claim: Research workflows and coding worktrees have different integration guarantees.

source.quote: Research workflows and coding worktrees have different integration guarantees

claims.reason: Descriptive, not a single testable property; the worktree half is exercised by verify-phase3-worktrees.mjs (scripted workers), the research half has no test that states its guarantee.

claims.claim: A custom URL or model name does not guarantee tool-call compatibility.

source.quote: A custom URL or a model name does not guarantee tool-call compatibility.

claims.claim: Full Access runs permitted commands with the owner's Windows account privileges and is not an OS sandbox.

source.quote: Full Access executes permitted commands with your Windows account privileges, not inside a universal OS sandbox.

claims.reason: Mixed sentence: it denies OS isolation but also says commands run with the owner's account privileges. verify-full-access.mjs checks the gate decision only (no approval, no workspace path check) with a hand-written workspace; no test runs a command in Full Access and shows whose privileges it has.

claims.claim: Worktrees are not OS isolation; host commands and supported Windows Sandbox verification give different assurance levels.

source.quote: Git worktrees provide checkout separation, **not operating-system isolation**; host commands and supported Windows Sandbox verification provide different assurance levels.

claims.reason: Mixed sentence: it denies OS isolation for worktrees but also says supported Windows Sandbox verification gives a different assurance level. The Windows Sandbox suites (verify-windows-sandbox-config.mjs, verify-sandbox-publisher.mjs) were not audited for the production seam.

claims.claim: Limits of the evidence for this release.

source.quote: In particular, an arbitrary custom Responses gateway has not been live-certified; a signed-in ChatGPT Edge session is not reproduced by scripted Chromium pages; host Git worktrees are not an OS sandbox.

claims.claim: Things the release does not claim.

source.quote: Live-model benchmark parity, offline Windows Sandbox certification, Authenticode signing and real-user browser account acceptance are **not claimed**.

claims.claim: The agent that started background agents is told when one stops and can read the agent's own final message, marked as that agent's claim, next to what the Hub recorded itself.

source.quote: It can then read what they produced with `agent_results`

claims.seamNote: A real Hub process over HTTP with real Git worktrees for the agents; only the model server is scripted (strict Chat Completions). The parent's answer is built from what the tool returned; a SIGKILL and restarts happen between the endings and the next run.
